Subject: Private Deploy Intake — environment cookbook & next steps

Jordan —

Great to meet you on the call yesterday. As discussed, I put together a concise 'intake cookbook' that maps our normal private deployment prerequisites to the Synthwell environment specifics so you can hand it to your infra team. The goal here is to make day-zero validation self-service and reduce back-and-forth.

What I'm attaching:
- redwood_privdeploy_cookbook_v1.pdf (summary + checklist)
- redwood_network_template.xlsx (CIDR / firewall / egress examples)

Can you confirm the following by EOD Monday so we can lock a Day0 window?
1) Team contact for network (name + slack/email)
2) Estimated maintenance blackout windows for next 14 days
3) Whether you want KMS keys managed in your account or by Redwood (we recommended customer-managed KMS for regulated data)

Karthik, Priyom — looped you in; please add anything we should require upfront beyond the cookbook for a Synthwell-style air-gapped segment.

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@synthwell.io>, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Deploy Intake — environment cookbook & next steps

Jordan / team —

Appreciate the quick responses. A couple of clarifications and an explicit preflight checklist we require before scheduling a Day0 provisioning window: 

Preflight checklist (please confirm each item):
- VPC: dedicated VPC or dedicated subnet in a customer VPC? (we strongly prefer dedicated VPC for isolation)
- CIDR ranges: confirm the CIDR ranges in the attached network template (we will use these for BGP / peer prep)
- Bastion/Jump: SSH bastion or SSM-based access? Provide bastion IP ranges if SSH
- Service accounts: service principal / IAM role allowed to create ENIs and SSM sessions (ARN needed)
- KMS: key ARN + key policy granting Redwood encryption/decryption from our account for bootstrap (customer-managed)
- Egress: explicit allowlist for telemetry endpoints — we only need to reach back to api.redwood.ai endpoints; list attached in the cookbook (80/443)
- Ports: internal inference ports (443, 2200 for controlled admin traffic) — if you run network inspection, please whitelist our health-check probes
- DNS: private hosted zone or resolvers we should use; we can optionally push split-horizon DNS entries during Day0

For air-gapped customers we take a slightly different approach — offline artifact bundles and a signed install package. If you plan to do an air-gap, we need those timelines at least 7 days in advance.

Action items:
- Jordan: send KMS ARN and the preferred VPC model by Thursday 12/9
- Priya (Synthwell): confirm bastion approach and add the network contact to the Drive link so we can track evidence
- Maya/Priyom (Redwood): we'll build a small preflight validation playbook and share it by EOD Friday 12/10

I'll attach the pared-down network template with recommended MTU and NAT rules — Maya, Priyom, feel free to edit before we share.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[karthik.iyer@redwood.ai]
